CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFAPPLICATION

CFAPPLICATION ties a page to a named application. Pages that use the same NAME share the Application scope, and, when you switch them on, each visitor gets their own Session and Client variables, recognized by the CFID and CFTOKEN cookies. The tag normally lives in Application.cfm, so that every page of the application runs it first.

Category

Application framework

Syntax

<CFAPPLICATION NAME="application_name"
    CLIENTMANAGEMENT="Yes/No"
    CLIENTSTORAGE="Registry/Cookie/datasource_name"
    SETCLIENTCOOKIES="Yes/No"
    SETDOMAINCOOKIES="Yes/No"
    SESSIONMANAGEMENT="Yes/No"
    SESSIONTIMEOUT="#CreateTimeSpan(days, hours, minutes, seconds)#"
    APPLICATIONTIMEOUT="#CreateTimeSpan(days, hours, minutes, seconds)#">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the application. The Application scope and the session/client data belong to it.
CLIENTMANAGEMENT
Optional, default "No". "Yes" enables the persistent Client scope.
CLIENTSTORAGE
Optional. Where client variables are kept: "Registry", "Cookie", or the name of a data source. The default is set on the Variables page of the Administrator.
SETCLIENTCOOKIES
Optional, default "Yes". "No" stops KoldFusion from sending the CFID and CFTOKEN cookies; you then have to pass Session.URLToken along in every link and form yourself.
SETDOMAINCOOKIES
Optional, default "No". Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
SESSIONMANAGEMENT
Optional, default "No". "Yes" enables the Session scope.
SESSIONTIMEOUT
Optional. How long an idle session lives, as a CreateTimeSpan value. The default (20 minutes) and the maximum are set on the Variables page of the Administrator.
APPLICATIONTIMEOUT
Optional. How long an idle application lives. Default and maximum (2 days) come from the Administrator.

Usage

A session is identified by Session.CFID and Session.CFTOKEN; Session.SessionID and Session.URLToken (ready to append to a URL as CFID=...&CFTOKEN=...) are set for you. Application.ApplicationName holds the NAME.

Application and session variables are shared between simultaneous requests, so read and write them inside CFLOCK blocks. Use CFERROR in the same Application.cfm to give the whole application a friendly error page.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFAPPLICATION NAME="KFSnippets"
    SESSIONMANAGEMENT="Yes"
    SESSIONTIMEOUT="#CreateTimeSpan(0, 0, 20, 0)#">

<CFLOCK SCOPE="Session" TYPE="Exclusive" TIMEOUT="10">
  <CFPARAM NAME="Session.Visits" DEFAULT="0">
  <CFSET Session.Visits = Session.Visits + 1>
  <CFSET Visits = Session.Visits>
  <CFSET Token = Session.URLToken>
</CFLOCK>

<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TD>Application.ApplicationName</TD><TD>#Application.ApplicationName#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Session.URLToken</TD><TD>#Token#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Visits in this session</TD><TD>#Visits#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P><A HREF="cfapplication.cfm">Reload</A> and watch the counter go up.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
